title: add prompt-recall-fidelity-scorer-and-granular-ci-thresholder
author: Evan Park
release_notes: Adds a prompt-level recall fidelity metric and a configurable CI thresholder that can soft-halt merges when prompt recall regressions are detected. Recommended for teams tracking reference preservation and citation recall in dialog/QA workloads.
description:
Motivation: We need a targeted, explainable signal for regressions where the model fails to preserve key referenced facts present in prompts (citations, referenced tools, explicit constraints). Current eval gates focus on overall accuracy/quality but miss cases where the model omits or rewrites referenced content. This PR introduces a Prompt Recall Fidelity (PRF) scorer and a granular CI thresholder that can be applied per-prompt-cohort with a soft-halt behavior to avoid blocking unrelated rollouts.

What this PR contains: 1) An efficient PRF scorer (eval_harness/metrics/prompt_recall_scorer.py) that computes a recall-style score combining token-level alignments, embedding overlap for paraphrase-tolerant matching, and a lightweight referent-extraction verifier for structured references (URLs, DOIs, code identifiers). 2) A CI adapter (ci/hooks/recall_thresholder.yml + eval_harness/ci/recall_thresholder.py) that takes cohort-level distributions and applies adaptive thresholds: per-cohort baseline + delta, with configurable soft-halt (mark PR as "soft-fail" and annotate with per-prompt evidence) and hard-fail escalation options. 3) Test coverage (tests/test_prompt_recall_scorer.py, tests/test_recall_thresholder_integration.py) with deterministic fixtures and a small synthetic suite that simulates hallucinated omission, paraphrase-preservation, and truncated output cases. 4) Docs and example (docs/eval/prompt_recall_fidelity.md) that explain metric semantics, recommended cohorts, and suggested thresholds for common families of workloads (FAQ/chat, citation-anchored QA, instruction-following).

Algorithmic notes: - Token alignment uses a fuzzy longest-common-subsequence weighted by wordpiece lengths to penalize dropped referents. - Embedding overlap uses precomputed sentence embeddings (cosine) with a simple calibration against positive/negative examples to be robust to paraphrase. - Structured referent verifier extracts deterministic tokens (URLs, hex ids, package names) and applies exact-match and prefix-match heuristics. - Final PRF score is a weighted combination: exact structured-match first, embedding overlap second, token alignment third; weights are configurable via YAML.

CI behavior and operator UX: - By default the CI hook runs as an optional check that reports mean/median PRF by cohort. Teams can enable strict mode (hard-fail) or soft-fail mode. Soft-fail annotates the PR with the lowest-scoring prompts (top K per cohort) and a suggested remediation: add a focused prompt-set or a targeted model variant test. - The thresholder supports time-windowed baselines (7/30/90d) and will automatically fall back to global baselines when cohort history is sparse. - When the check triggers, the CI comment includes inline evidence: prompt id, expected references, model output excerpt, PRF score, and nearest-match embedding snippets.

Commit summary: - commit 1: initial PRF scorer implementation and unit tests - commit 2: integrate structured referent extractor and embedding calibration - commit 3: CI adapter + thresholder operational config and GitHub check reporter - commit 4: docs, example cohorts, and cli wrapper for local run - commit 5: test hardening and threshold defaults tuning after review feedback

Changed files (high level): ["eval_harness/metrics/prompt_recall_scorer.py", "eval_harness/metrics/_helpers/structured_referent_extractor.py", "eval_harness/ci/recall_thresholder.py", "ci/hooks/recall_thresholder.yml", "tests/test_prompt_recall_scorer.py", "tests/test_recall_thresholder_integration.py", "docs/eval/prompt_recall_fidelity.md", "examples/recall_cohorts/example_cohorts.yml", "eval_harness/cli/run_recall_check.py", "eval_harness/metrics/embeddings_calibrator.py", "eval_harness/ci/reporting/recall_reporter.py", "pyproject.toml"]

Selected snippets: - recall_thresholder.yml declares thresholds per-cohort and maps to Linear keys for escalation - prompt_recall_scorer.py exposes a score() function that accepts (prompt_text, model_output, reference_tokens) and returns {"prf": float, "evidence": [..]} (See docs for schema).

Review conversation (high-level thread): - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Nice focused metric. Please add a unit test for structured referent extractor when multiple referents share token prefixes (e.g., pkg-1 and pkg-10). Also we should avoid expensive embedding computations in the fast path." - Evan Park (author): "Added targeted unit for prefix collisions and moved embedding calibrator to an async background cache with TTL; cheap fingerprinting allows early-exit for exact matches." - Jordan Liu (reviewer): "Can we expose a debug mode that dumps per-prompt alignment traces to help SRE triage failures?" - Evan Park: "Added debug flag to CLI and a retention param for CI artifact upload; default off to avoid large artifacts." - Priya Raman (approver): "Tests and docs look good. Suggest default soft-fail for non-enterprise orgs." - Maya Chen: "Left one minor comment about logging levels, addressed in follow-up commit."

CI summary: - Initial run: 2 flaky test failures (timing-sensitive embedding cache test) -> rerun triggered - Final run: all checks pass (unit tests, integration smoke, lint). Performance: PRF scoring runs at ~1.8ms per prompt on our small benchmark (single-vCPU) after cache warmup; acceptable as a CI check.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind a feature flag: eval.PRF_ENABLED=false by default. - Enable in staging CI for core teams for 2 weeks to collect baselines. - After baseline collection, recommend targets per-cohort and flip soft-fail on for teams that want stricter gating.

Backward compatibility and risks: - Non-breaking: default: disabled feature flag and conservative defaults. - Risk: poor thresholds may generate noisy soft-fails; mitigated by per-cohort baselines, configurable smoothing, and sample-size requirements (min n=30).

Related tickets: ENG-721 (collect prompt-level annotations), ENG-732 (CI gate infra enhancements).
